title: Launch Day
tagline: Every new product needs a page, a sticker, a guide and a date.
what: When something new ships, whether it is a product, a software release or a new program, I get everything around it ready: the page, the labels, the inserts, the guide and the day-of checklist.
does: Launch new products, kits and accessories: page, photos, options, price, stock
Ship software and firmware releases with notes, a what's-new page and an email
Run beta, trade-up, dealer and partner programs from plan to announcement
Design warning, safety and product stickers, and cut down how many kinds we keep
Write and design the inserts that ship in the box, with a spec sheet for reorders
Draw box artwork to fit the foam, checked with purchasing
Print prototypes in house, test the fit and vet vendor samples
Run the day-of checklist: stock in, products live, test order, email out

solved.problem: A big firmware release had to hit the site, the product options and customers' inboxes together.
solved.did: Got the new pages ready ahead of time so they could go live together, and held the email until engineering finished testing.
solved.ended: It went live in two stages, with a beta label on the new version.

solved.problem: The warehouse kept eight to ten kinds of stickers on hand for modules and firmware.
solved.did: Cut the set down to a few, and built a page that prints serial and address stickers on the label printer.
solved.ended: A warehouse tech tested it on their own printer and it went into daily use.

solved.problem: A beta product needed a part that fit snugly with no glue.
solved.did: Printed and refined a filler part until it fit to a fraction of a millimetre, then made a batch.
solved.ended: The beta units went out to field testers.

worksWith: Leadership, customer service, the warehouse, purchasing, finance, a developer, a contract designer, printers and vendors.
story: The finished welcome packets were in my hands before the biggest sale of the year, ready to go into customers' boxes: a set of cards, a decal and a proper envelope.
The box had held separate inserts made at different times. I wanted one packet that felt like it belonged together.

I got quotes at a few print quantities and put design options in front of leadership. Once they picked one, I wrote a master spec sheet with leadership and customer service so reorders use the same files and sizes.
I ran a sample and checked that the printed codes scanned. Then I placed the order and tracked it in. The decal stayed in the kit as the piece people could hold on to.
